entities.summary: The swing revival, also called retro swing and neo-swing, was a renewed interest in swing music and Lindy Hop dance, beginning around 1989 and reaching a peak in the 1990s. The music was generally rooted in the big bands of the swing era of the 1930s and 1940s, but it was also greatly influenced by rockabilly, boogie-woogie, the jump blues of artists such as Louis Prima and Louis Jordan, and the theatrics of Cab Calloway. Many neo-swing bands practiced contemporary fusions of swing, jazz, and jump blues with rock, punk rock, ska, and ska punk music or had roots in punk, ska, ska punk, and alternative rock music.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The swing revival of the late 20th century influenced a new generation of musicians and dancers, contributing to the preservation of traditional swing music and dance styles. Its impact can be seen in the continued popularity of big bands and Lindy Hop events today.
